### Project Name

bbot and the Agent Face Protocol (AFP)

### Project Description

bbot gives AI agents a face that people can read at a glance. It has three parts:

- **Agent Face Protocol (AFP)**, a small, transport-agnostic JSON format for an agent to show what it is doing (`thinking`, `working`, `waiting`, `error`…), how it feels about it (30 expressions), one-shot reactions (`nod`, `shake`…) and speech with lip-sync. Every expression has a plain-language gloss, so the same signal works as a face, a caption or screen-reader text. Spec: https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/tree/main/spec
- **bbot**, the reference renderer: a dependency-free JavaScript library (MIT, about 5 kB gzipped) on npm as [`@bwnd/bbot`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@bwnd/bbot).
- **The bbot desktop widget**, a reference host: an always-on-top Electron face that chats through any model on OpenRouter, speaks through ElevenLabs, acts the conversation out and offers MCP-shaped local file tools.

**Origin:** built in the open by blue wind (bwnd.app) starting in August 2026. The first npm release was on 31 August 2026, and there have been eight releases since. The spec was drafted in October 2026 to separate the vocabulary from the drawing.

### Preferred Lifecycle Stage (if known)

Sandbox

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

Agents increasingly work for minutes at a time: reasoning, calling tools, waiting for approval, failing and recovering. AFP gives them a neutral, honest way to show that state to people, which improves the observability and trustworthiness of agentic systems at the point where humans actually look. Its value is interoperability: one vocabulary that any agent can emit and any renderer can draw. That needs neutral governance before vendor-specific "mood" fields take hold.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

- **MCP:** AFP defines an MCP binding (`face_state`, `face_express`, `face_react`, `face_look`, `face_speak`), so any MCP client can drive a face through tool calls. The bbot site already ships an MCP server for rendering faces, and the widget's desktop tools are MCP-shaped.
- **goose and other agent hosts:** a natural first integration is a goose extension that maps agent state (thinking, tool use, errors) to AFP.
- **AGENTS.md / Agent Skills:** bbot publishes a `SKILL.md` and `llms.txt` so coding agents can add a face to an app unaided.

AFP does not overlap with any current AAIF project. It sits on the human-facing edge of them.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

**Use cases:** showing a coding agent's state in an IDE or desktop; a face for voice agents with lip-sync; customer-facing chat assistants; accessible agent status (gloss text for screen readers); avatar and robot renderers driven by any agent.

**Early external interest (stated honestly):** 47 GitHub stars; 220 unique repository visitors in 14 days, about 140 of them from one Threads post; about 340 jsDelivr CDN loads of the npm build in the last month. npm reports about 1,250 monthly downloads, but we treat that figure as noisy. There are no known third-party AFP implementations yet. Getting them is the first Sandbox goal. See the thesis for why this matters before adoption: https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/THESIS.md

### License

MIT

### Governance Model

Maintainer-led, documented in https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md. Library changes need one maintainer's approval. Spec changes are proposed as an issue labelled `spec`, stay open for at least 14 days, and need a majority of maintainers. Disagreements go to a maintainer majority vote. The stated top priority is adding maintainers from other organisations. We are happy to adopt LF Minimum Viable Governance on admission.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

GitHub Actions runs on every push and pull request (Node 20 and 22): `npm ci`, `npm run build` (esbuild), `npm test` (node:test; checks the spec and library vocabularies agree, poses stay in range and reactions are numerically stable). A maintainer releases to npm from a clean checkout of the repo and tags each release (`v0.6.1`). There have been eight releases since 31 August 2026.

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md: spec changes start as a public issue using the `spec` template, are open for comment for at least 14 days, then merge on a maintainer majority. Breaking changes bump the spec's major version. Commits are signed off under the DCO.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/issues

### External Project Dependencies

- Library: none at runtime. Optional peer dependency: React ≥17 (MIT).
- Build: esbuild (MIT).
- Desktop widget: Electron (MIT), ws (MIT). Optional third-party services, used with the user's own keys: OpenRouter (chat), ElevenLabs (voice).

### Maintainers & Contributors

- **James** ([bookofone](https://github.com/bookofone)), blue wind: lead maintainer for the library, widget and spec. [Commits](https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/commits?author=bookofone)
- **bwnd** ([bwndapp](https://github.com/bwndapp)), blue wind: project account, releases

Full list: https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md. Both are currently affiliated with blue wind. Recruiting a maintainer from another organisation is a stated Sandbox goal.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

James (bookofone, blue wind) leads the project. Decisions follow GOVERNANCE.md (see Governance Model above).

### Lifecycle Stage Evidence

Sandbox thesis (intended users, Growth criteria, early interest and the case before adoption): https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/THESIS.md

Sandbox criteria: OSI-approved permissive licence (MIT) ✓ · working implementation (library, spec, desktop host, published on npm) ✓ · one actively committing maintainer with documented intent to grow the contributor base (GOVERNANCE.md) ✓ · written thesis ✓. The 6–12 month roadmap is in the thesis.

### Security

No OpenSSF Best Practices badge yet; we will apply. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled on GitHub, and the policy is in https://github.com/bwndapp/bbot/blob/main/SECURITY.md (acknowledgement within 5 working days). The library takes no network input. The desktop widget's file tools are read-only and confined to folders the user picks. CI runs with read-only permissions.

### Infrastructure Needs or Requests

Standard Sandbox infrastructure only: a repository home under the foundation's GitHub organisation, and CI.

### Additional Information

AFP is deliberately small: six message types and a fixed, glossed vocabulary. We'd rather it be easy to implement than complete. Open questions (expression intensity, namespaced extensions, valence/arousal fallback) are listed in the spec for public discussion.
